verdict.rationale: Hyperbrowser is an AI browser-automation platform (HyperAgent's page.ai, agents), so caching resolved actions for deterministic replay is a fair question. However, nothing in the evidence documents caching LLM-resolved actions or generated code for replay. The closest items are adjacent and earn no credit: Profiles persist browser state such as cookies and cache, and session recordings (rrweb/MP4) replay sessions for debugging, not for re-executing actions without the LLM.

support.subject: As a developer, I can cache resolved actions or generated code so repeat runs replay deterministically at lower cost and latency than re-prompting the LLM
